derivedPrompt: Convert the production walkthrough for Neon Alone into an original Neon Studio project. Carry over the described arrangement (Production Notes, Second Drop, Intro, Verse, Build, Intro), track roles (lead, chords, drums, bass, hat, automation), and production techniques, but keep the result original and portable.

gaps.label: High-pass everything that is not the low end
gaps.why: Every melodic and FX layer carries low rumble that adds up into the 200-500 Hz range, which is exactly where the checker reports mud.
gaps.step: Give each lane a high-pass: chords 180 Hz, lead 220 Hz (250 in the drop), plucks 250 Hz, vocals 150 Hz, guitars 120 Hz, FX/risers/noise/crashes 300 Hz. Only the kick, sub and bass are exempt. Record it as a mix note so the renderer and a human agree.

gaps.label: Keep the bottom mono
gaps.why: Widened low frequencies partially cancel when the track is played in mono, so the bass disappears on phones and club systems.
gaps.step: State a mono crossover — 110 Hz for house, 130 for future bass and modern EDM, 150 for darker bass music — and mark the kick, sub and bass lanes mono. Apply every widener, chorus and reverb send after the lane's high-pass, never before it.

gaps.label: Decide what is allowed to be wide
gaps.why: When every layer is widened, nothing sounds wide, the centre hollows out, and stereo correlation drops far enough for the checker to flag it.
gaps.step: Assign each lane a width tier: centre-locked (kick, sub, bass, snare body, the main hook), mid 0.25-0.40 (chords, hats, plucks), wide 0.60-0.80 (the lead octave double, vocal chops, FX, reverb returns). Keep no more than two or three lanes wide at once.

gaps.label: Set a level ladder and a peak budget
gaps.why: With no target levels the render is balanced by whatever the generator's defaults happen to be, which is how a mix ends up either quiet or squashed.
gaps.step: Write lane offsets relative to the kick: kick 0 dB, sub -2, bass -5, lead -4, clap -6, chords -7, vocal -8, plucks -12, FX -12, hats -14. Set a master ceiling of -1.0 dBFS and allow only the drop within a dB of it.

gaps.label: Stop the drums repeating bar for bar
gaps.why: The renderer reuses an unscoped pattern for every bar, so without bar-scoped events the sixteenth bar of a drop is identical to the first.
gaps.step: Scope some drum events to particular bars: an open hat on odd bars, a kick dropped on the last beat of bar 4, an extra clap on bar 6. Small differences, but they stop the pattern reading as a loop.

gaps.label: Give every named part something to play
gaps.why: A role listed in a section but never given events becomes a track with no clips: the project looks fuller than it sounds, and the checker reports it as missing audio.
gaps.step: For each role with no lane events, either write a starter pattern for it or take it out of the section. An empty lane is worse than an absent one, because it hides the fact that the part was never made.

gaps.label: Derive every melodic part from one idea
gaps.why: Unrelated melodies in the intro, drop and break give a song three identities and no hook; one idea restated is what makes an arrangement cohere.
gaps.step: Pick the drop's hook as canonical and derive the rest from it: the intro states a truncated filtered version, the break plays it slower or on a different instrument, the outro plays its first two notes. Same idea, different treatment.
